headline: Man Spends 847 Hours Commenting 'Here Before This Blows Up' on Six-Year-Old Posts
subheadline: Local resident's dedication to premature viral prediction spans multiple platforms and time zones
summary: A Millbrook man has been identified as the person behind thousands of 'here before viral' comments on years-old content across every major platform.
content:
The comment appears with eerie consistency across the internet's forgotten corners: "Here before this blows up" followed by a confident emoji.

The author of these prophetic messages has finally been identified as Gerald Hutchins, 34, a data entry specialist from Millbrook who has spent an estimated 847 hours over the past two years commenting on dormant content.

"Everyone wants to be the person who called it," Hutchins explained in an interview conducted at his home, surrounded by multiple monitors displaying various social media feeds. "But they're all competing for the same new posts. I'm playing a different game."

Hutchins' strategy involves seeking out posts from 2018 or earlier that have received minimal engagement, then leaving his signature comment in anticipation of future virality.

"Statistically, something has to eventually resurface," he reasoned. "And when it does, I'll already be there. Waiting."

A deep dive into his comment history reveals a staggering commitment. Threadit posts about discontinued snacks, VidTube videos with 12 views, Chirper threads about forgotten memes, all bear his mark.

"I found his comment on a 2017 video about fidget spinners," reported internet archaeologist Sandra Pine. "The video has 847 views total. His comment has been there for 14 months. He's still waiting."

Hutchins maintains detailed spreadsheets tracking each comment, including the post date, his comment date, and current engagement metrics. The success rate column remains empty.

"Not yet," he clarified when asked about wins. "Not yet. But virality is unpredictable. The Threadit post about that old car commercial could resurface tomorrow. And I'll have commented 'here before this blows up' 847 days before everyone else."

Psychologists have expressed mild concern about the behavior, though Hutchins insists it's purely recreational.

"It's like buying lottery tickets," he said. "Except the lottery is other people's old content suddenly becoming popular, and my ticket is a comment that will make me look prescient."

When asked what he would actually gain if one of his predictions came true, Hutchins paused for a long moment.

"I guess people would see the comment and think 'wow, this guy knew,'" he said finally. "That's enough."

His most recent comment was left on a 2019 ClipTok video of someone's cat sneezing. It has four views.
author: Diana Frost, Human Interest
